artworks.title: Primavera
artworks.description: In Botticelli's allegory of spring in the Uffizi, Flora stands at the right in a flower-strewn gown, scattering blossoms as Zephyrus seizes Chloris behind her — Ovid's Fasti transformed into a Florentine garden of eternal May. The Roman flower-goddess becomes the painting's most recognizable figure of seasonal return.

artworks.title: Flora
artworks.description: Titian's half-length goddess in the Uffizi holds roses and jasmine against loose white linen — Flora as Venetian beauty rather than calendar rite. The soft light and open bodice made this one of the Renaissance's most copied images of the flower goddess.

artworks.title: Flora
artworks.description: Rembrandt paints his bride Saskia as Flora: staff, flowers, and a soft Amsterdam light that turns the Roman goddess into a private wedding allegory. The Hermitage canvas remains one of the most intimate modern faces given to the Sabine flower deity.

artworks.title: The Triumph of Flora
artworks.description: Poussin's Louvre triumph stages Flora in a chariot amid putti and blooming nymphs — a classical procession of spring drawn from Ovid and Roman festival memory. Order, dance, and flowers fuse the goddess with the season she governs.

artworks.title: The Return of Spring
artworks.description: Bouguereau's Joslyn Art Museum canvas surrounds a nude Flora with putti and blossoms — academic spring as the goddess's bodily return. The painting made Flora a late-Victorian emblem of seasonal rebirth for American audiences.

popCulture.title: Fasti
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book 5 of Ovid's calendar poem gives Flora her voice: the Sabine flower-goddess who tells how she helped Juno conceive Mars, and why Rome keeps the Floralia.
